questions.prompt: A Standard App Service app has www.example.com mapped with verified DNS. A valid private certificate covering that hostname is uploaded. A browser connects directly to App Service using that hostname but does not receive the uploaded certificate. Which configuration associates this hostname with that certificate?

options.text: Add an SNI TLS binding for www.example.com using the uploaded certificate.
options.explanation: The hostname-to-certificate binding selects the certificate for the custom HTTPS endpoint; uploading it alone does not establish that association.

options.text: Enable HTTPS Only without adding a certificate binding.
options.explanation: HTTPS Only redirects HTTP to HTTPS; it does not select the uploaded certificate for the custom hostname.

options.text: Set the app minimum TLS version to 1.2 without adding a binding.
options.explanation: A protocol minimum limits permitted TLS versions, not which certificate is associated with the hostname.

options.text: Add a binding for api.example.com using the uploaded certificate.
options.explanation: A binding for a different hostname does not associate the certificate with the requested www.example.com endpoint.

questions.prompt: A Standard App Service app must secure mapped first-level subdomains with a certificate covering *.example.com. Clients require a publicly trusted certificate. Which certificate acquisition and binding approach meets the wildcard requirement?

options.text: Upload a trusted wildcard private certificate as a compliant PFX, then bind it to the mapped hostnames.
options.explanation: A private certificate that includes the private key, required chain, and wildcard coverage can secure the mapped first-level subdomains through TLS bindings.

options.text: Create a free App Service managed wildcard certificate, then bind it to the mapped hostnames.
options.explanation: Free App Service managed certificates do not support wildcard names; this requested certificate cannot be issued through that option.

options.text: Reuse the platform certificate for the default azurewebsites.net hostname on the mapped hostnames.
options.explanation: The platform default-hostname certificate does not cover the custom example.com subdomains.

options.text: Upload only the wildcard public certificate without its private key, then use it for the hostname bindings.
options.explanation: A public certificate upload is for use in application code, not securing custom domains. Server-side TLS requires a compliant private certificate.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of an SNI TLS binding in App Service?

options.text: Select the hostname certificate from the server name sent during the TLS handshake, allowing a shared IP.
options.explanation: SNI conveys the requested server name during TLS so multiple hostname certificates can be served on the same IP.

options.text: Select the hostname certificate from a dedicated destination IP without requiring a server name.
options.explanation: That describes IP-based TLS selection; SNI permits hostname selection on a shared IP.

options.text: Select the hostname certificate from the URL path sent after the TLS handshake.
options.explanation: The TLS certificate must be selected during the handshake, before the encrypted HTTP request supplies its path.

options.text: Select the hostname certificate from the client source IP during the TLS handshake.
options.explanation: SNI identifies the requested server hostname, not the client source address.
